subject: general
question: Which of following silver coins was introduced by Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tanka was a silver coin introduced by Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish in the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Iltutmish issued the Tanka in the early 13th century as a part of his currency reforms.
 
• The Tanka weighed about 175 grains (approximately 11 grams) of silver.
 
• This coinage system set the standard for the currency in the Indian subcontinent during the medieval period.
 
• The introduction of the Tanka helped stabilize the economy and facilitated trade within the Sultanate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iltutmish:** Shamsuddin Iltutmish was the third ruler of the Mamluk dynasty in Delhi, known for his administrative and military strategies.
 
• **Currency Reforms:** Iltutmish's introduction of the Tanka and Jittal (copper coins) was part of his effort to streamline and standardize the currency system.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The Tanka contributed significantly to the economic development of the Delhi Sultanate by facilitating trade and commerce.
 
• **Historical Significance:** The Tanka remained in use even after the fall of the Delhi Sultanate, influencing the coinage of subsequent dynasties.
 
• **Standardization:** The weight and purity standards set by the Tanka were adhered to by later rulers, ensuring consistency in the monetary system.
